officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms -t/--test-name-pattern is a regex name filter. The docs do NOT specify a non-zero exit when the pattern matches zero tests; probed empirically on 1.3.13 and it exits 0 with 'matched 0 tests', so a bare -t oracle is zero-match-vacuous and MUST be guarded by asserting a non-zero 'N pass' summary line. Docs also confirm that under CLAUDECODE=1 (the worker env) passing-test indicators are hidden but 'Summary statistics remain intact'; probed and the 'N pass' line does survive, so the guard holds in worker sessions.

userStories.title: Add the frozen-comparand OracleLintRule
userStories.description: As a planner-dispatch gate, I need a pure rule that flags an oracle comparing against a literal integer read off main with no live re-derivation token, so that the derive-don't-freeze rule at patterns.md:903 is enforced before dispatch instead of rotting silently mid-cycle.
acceptanceCriteria: A FROZEN_COMPARAND_RULE is exported from src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts and registered in the RULES array. RED-ON-MAIN (swept: identifier absent on main). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'FROZEN_COMPARAND_RULE' src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts]

The rule is proven falsifiable in the defect direction by a dedicated describe block whose tests actually run (non-vacuous: a bare -t exits 0 on zero matches, so the 'N pass' summary is asserted). RED-ON-MAIN (swept: describe block absent on main). [oracle: named-command bun test test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts -t 'frozen-comparand rule: flagged forms' 2>&1 | grep -qE '^ *[1-9][0-9]* pass']

The rule is proven non-firing in the corrected direction, including a criterion carrying a live `git show main:` derivation alongside an integer, by a dedicated describe block whose tests actually run. RED-ON-MAIN (swept: describe block absent on main). [oracle: named-command bun test test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts -t 'frozen-comparand rule: passing cases' 2>&1 | grep -qE '^ *[1-9][0-9]* pass']

Deliberately GREEN on main: labelled invariance/pinning guard. The module's no-I/O purity contract holds across the whole Bun surface, not just imports: no node:fs / node:child_process / fs/promises / bun: / `from 'bun'` import, and no Bun.file / Bun.spawn / Bun.$ / Bun.write call on a code line. Scoped to code lines so a comment DOCUMENTING the no-I/O contract cannot trip it. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qE "^import .*(node:fs|node:child_process|fs/promises|bun:|from ['\"]bun['\"])" src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts && ! grep -qE '^[^/]*Bun\.(file|spawn|\$|write)' src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: named-command bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: named-command bun test]
Full quality spine green. [oracle: named-command bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts (add rule + register in RULES at ~:135), test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts. REUSE parseOracleDirectives from src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts; never write a second criterion parser (issue gotcha). PURITY: every rule must be decidable from the criterion string alone, the walk performs no I/O (module header contract). TEST NAMING IS LOAD-BEARING: the oracles above match `describe('frozen-comparand rule: flagged forms', ...)` and `describe('frozen-comparand rule: passing cases', ...)` verbatim, mirroring the existing grep-q-plus-list-files blocks at test lines 44/94; deviating from that naming makes the story's own oracles vacuous. Rule shape: flag an integer comparand (-eq/-ge/-le/== N, `wc -l` compared to a literal) when NO live re-derivation token (`git show main:`, `git grep ... main`, `git diff main`) appears in the SAME criterion. patterns.md:903 is the source bullet. Guard noUncheckedIndexedAccess on every regex capture group.

acceptanceCriteria: A ZERO_MATCH_VACUOUS_RULE is exported from src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts and registered in the RULES array. RED-ON-MAIN (swept: identifier absent on main). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'ZERO_MATCH_VACUOUS_RULE' src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts]

[oracle: named-command M=$(git show main:src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts | awk '/export const RULES: OracleLintRule\[\] =/,/\];/' | grep -o '[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_RULE' | wc -l); B=$(awk '/export const RULES: OracleLintRule\[\] =/,/\];/' src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts | grep -o '[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_RULE' | wc -l); test $((B-M)) -eq 3]

BOTH test directions were actually written for all three new rules, asserted structurally rather than by a command that a one-directional test set would also satisfy: the branch adds exactly 3 'flagged forms' describe blocks AND exactly 3 'passing cases' describe blocks over main, both sides derived live. RED-ON-MAIN (swept: both deltas are 0 on unmodified main, exit 1). userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts, test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts. TEST NAMING IS LOAD-BEARING: `zero-match-vacuous rule: flagged forms` / `zero-match-vacuous rule: passing cases`, and the cumulative AC5 requires US-001 and US-002 to have used their own exact names too, so do not rename earlier blocks. COVERAGE-DELTA DERIVATION, measured decision: the issue's AC8 suggests deriving main's PASS count via a run against main state, but that was probed and is UNSOUND here: a detached `git worktree` at main with node_modules symlinked yields 5185 pass / 7 FAIL while the same commit in the real repo yields 5192 pass / 0 fail, because ~7 tests are cwd/environment-sensitive. Comparing an in-repo branch run to a worktree main run would compare apples to oranges and would spuriously FLATTER the branch by ~+7. The static declaration count above is environment-independent, derives both sides live via git refs, and was probed falsifiable (excluding one test file drops it 4906 -> 4886, exit 1). Do NOT reintroduce a worktree-run baseline, and do NOT write any baseline file into src/ (an earlier draft wrote src/supervisor/.main-baseline-lint.ts, which is not gitignored and would leak into `git add -A`; the git-ref derivation above needs no temp file at all). Source bullet: patterns.md:901.

userStories.notes: Files: .claude/agents/subagent-auditor.md (item 9 at ~:67-72), templates/agents/subagent-auditor.md (same item at ~:64-69, DIFFERENT line numbers: anchor by content, never by line). The two files DIFFER overall by three deliberate cam-cli specialization hunks (dependency-ordering tiers, Ink/terminal-only verification, invariants section): do NOT reconcile those. Only item 9 is in scope and only item 9 is byte-identical (verified: 6 lines each, cmp-clean today). templates/ is embedded into the binary via src/vendor/_generated.ts, so `bun run embed-vendor` is REQUIRED (AC3 fails otherwise); .claude/agents/*.md is read from disk at spawn and needs no rebuild. The rule is deliberately PROSE not a lint rule: executing a candidate oracle needs shell plus a worktree and would break prd-oracle-lint.ts's no-I/O contract (issue gotcha, an accepted structural limit, must not be 'fixed' by adding I/O to that module).
